title: Watchkeeping and Bridge Team Procedures
description: The TDPO learns the standards required for sustained DP watchkeeping — monitoring discipline, log entry practice, and formal watch handover procedure. Professional standard means the TDPO monitors all critical parameters at regular intervals without prompting, makes complete and timely log entries, and can conduct a full handover covering every required item.

tasks.title: Sustained Position Keeping Observation
tasks.vessel_mode_execute: DP — observe only unless safety issue
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP in moderate conditions. DPO will gradually increase environmental conditions during the observation period. Your role is monitor and assess — do not intervene unless a genuine safety issue develops.
tasks.execute: Monitor the DP system holding position for 30 minutes while conditions increase. Record position footprint, thruster demand, reference quality, and current vector at 5-minute intervals. Identify any trends. Assess at what point intervention would be required. At each 5-minute mark write your observation before looking at the previous entry — do not let previous readings anchor your assessment.
professional_standard: All parameters recorded at every 5-minute interval without prompting
Correct intervention threshold identified with reasoning
Assessment does not simply mirror the previous reading

variants.title: Sustained Observation Near Structure
variants.note_to_tdpo: Same observation but with a virtual structure at 100m. Degrading conditions now have a direct safety consequence. Your intervention threshold assessment is no longer theoretical.

tasks.title: DP Watch Handover
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP in moderate conditions with a virtual structure active at 100m. A realistic handover scenario — the incoming DPO needs everything.
tasks.execute: Part 1 — Give handover: You are the outgoing DPO. Brief your DPO on full system status covering every checklist item. Vessel position and heading, mode and setpoint, reference systems and quality, sensor status, thruster configuration, power configuration, environmental conditions, nearby structures and working side, alarms active or recently cleared, any system degradation, operational requirements for the next watch. Part 2 — Receive handover: Swap roles. Receive a handover from your DPO. Ask all questions you would ask as an incoming DPO. Identify any gaps in what you were told.
professional_standard: All handover items covered without prompting
Minimum 5 questions asked as incoming DPO
Gaps in received handover correctly identified
Refusal to accept an incomplete handover demonstrated

fields.label: Items covered in handover you gave — list them
Items DPO identified as missed in your handover
Questions you asked when receiving handover
Gaps identified in the handover you received
Would you have accepted the watch based on the handover you received? Why or why not?
Notes

debrief_questions: What items did you miss in the handover you gave — and are those items safety-critical?
Under what circumstances would you refuse to accept a watch handover?
What is the single most important piece of information in a DP watch handover?
How does a DP watch handover differ from a standard bridge watchkeeping handover?

variants.title: Handover with Degraded System
variants.note_to_tdpo: DPO will introduce a system degradation before the handover — one reference inhibited, one thruster on standby, an alarm cleared but not resolved. You must identify all degradations in the handover you receive and decide whether to accept.

tasks.title: DP Log Entry Discipline
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP. Paper and pen ready for log entries. DPO will trigger events during a 20-minute period without announcing what or when. Your job is to log everything correctly.
tasks.execute: During the 20-minute period your DPO will trigger several events — a reference quality degradation, a wind increase, a thruster loading change, and a position alert. For each event make a DP log entry in the correct format: time, event description, action taken, system status after action. DPO assesses completeness and accuracy of all entries at the end.
professional_standard: Every event logged within 2 minutes of occurrence
All required fields completed for each entry
Action taken clearly stated for each entry

Notes

debrief_questions: What information is mandatory in every DP log entry — what are the minimum required fields?
Why is timestamp accuracy critical in a DP log — what happens to your log if a DP incident occurs?
What constitutes an event worthy of a log entry versus routine monitoring that does not need logging?
Who reads your DP log entries after an incident — and how should that knowledge affect how you write them?

variants.title: Log Entries Under Pressure
variants.note_to_tdpo: Same exercise but DPO will trigger multiple events in quick succession. Logging discipline under time pressure is harder than when events are spaced out. Prioritise — what gets logged first?
